title: etbb-july-2024-may-2025-update.pdf — section 146
text:
158. The Inns of Court College of Advocacy have produced training for advocates which has also
been used by the Judicial College, with a useful set of principles of questioning and conduct,
which should normally be adopted.107

159. Before any topic is introduced, the witness should be given a headline telling them what the
topic is, eg: “I am going to ask you questions about when you were nine”, or “I am going to
ask you questions about what happened in the shed”.

160. During questioning:
• Pronouns should not be used. When referring to a person, the name of the person should
be used on every occasion.
• Questions should be simple and contain only one matter. There should be no compound
questions.

103 R v Wills [2011] EWCA Crim 1938.

104 See guidance in R v YGM [2018] EWCA Crim 2458.

105 Rule 3(11)d Criminal Procedure Rules 2020.
